__comment__: EconomyX — phone hold poses. ONE file drives all 26 phones, because every
phone geometry uses a single bone named 'phone'.
WHICH WAY DOES THE PHONE FACE
Read off the geometry, not guessed: in every one of the 9 phone models the
camera-bump cubes sit at negative Z (they protrude past the body's -0.5 to
-Z  (north face) = the BACK of the phone, with the cameras
+Z  (south face) = the SCREEN
In Bedrock item-bone space -Z points the way the holder is facing. At yaw 0
the cameras therefore point away from the holder — out at everyone else —
and the screen points back at the holder. That is exactly the behaviour we
want in both views, which is why both poses below use a Y rotation of 0.
Rotating Y by 180 would swap it: screen out, cameras at your own face.
WHY THESE POSITIONS
The pack's 55 playing cards render correctly at first-person position
[-1.5, 5.5, 1.5] and third-person [0, 3.0, 0], so those are known-good hand
coordinates. The card's geometry starts at y=0, but a phone's geometry runs
from y=-5.28 up to y=+11.22 — the origin is at the lower third, where a hand
actually grips. Roughly a third of the phone therefore hangs BELOW the bone
origin, and the first-person Y is lifted to 6.5 so that overhang does not
drop out of the visible frame. The previous values put the origin at y=1.0,
which pushed the whole handset below the first-person view — the phone was
being drawn, just not anywhere you could see it.
TUNING — grip poses always want a nudge or two once you see them in game.
Edit ONLY this file; nothing else references these numbers.
phone clips into the arm ............ raise position[1], or lower scale
phone hangs below the screen edge ... raise position[1]
you see the cameras, not the screen . set rotation[1] to 180
phone lies flat instead of upright .. move rotation[0] toward 0
sits too far left/right of the hand . adjust position[0]
